Metadata.Summary: Derm Foundation is a machine learning model designed to accelerate AI development for skin image analysis in dermatology applications using pre-trained embeddings. It produces a 6144-dimensional embedding vector as output for downstream tasks like classifying skin conditions and scoring severity.
Metadata.Keywords: machine learning; dermatology; skin image analysis; embeddings; AI

UsesAndDirections.IntendedUseAndWorkflow: Derm Foundation reduces the data, compute, and expertise needed to develop task-specific models for skin image analysis. Embeddings can be used for classifying conditions, scoring severity, identifying body parts, and determining image quality.
UsesAndDirections.PrimaryIntendedUsers: Businesses and institutions in healthcare and life sciences, researchers
UsesAndDirections.HowToUse: Use code snippets and Colab notebooks to run the model locally or create a production version using Model Garden.

Warnings.ModelLimitations: Derm Foundation's quality can degrade in extreme lighting/noise. It was trained on data from a limited set of countries (US, Colombia, Australia, public images) and may not generalize well to other countries, populations, or image types. The model only generates embeddings and does not make predictions or diagnoses.

TrustIngredients.OutcomesAndOutput: The model produces a 6144-dimensional embedding vector as output, which can be used for downstream tasks.
TrustIngredients.TypeAndValueOfSolutionOutput: Embedding vector of floating point values (Dimensions: 6144)
TrustIngredients.ExplanationForHowAnOutputIsGenerated: Derm Foundation is pre-trained on large amounts of labeled skin images to produce 6144 dimensional embeddings that capture dense features relevant for analyzing these images.
TrustIngredients.InputDataSource: A large number of health-related image-text pairs from the public web and tele-dermatology datasets from the United States and Colombia, a skin cancer dataset from Australia, and additional public images.
TrustIngredients.OutputInputDataType: Input: PNG image file 448 x 448 pixels

UsefulnessEfficacy.GoalOfMetrics: Derm Foundation was evaluated for data-efficient accuracy across a range of skin-related classifications tasks [SOURCE 1]
UsefulnessEfficacy.Result: Training a linear classifier on Derm-Foundations embeddings were substantially more performant (10-15% increase in accuracy) than doing the same for a standard BiT-M model across different proportions of training data [SOURCE 1]
UsefulnessEfficacy.Interpretation: Models built on top of the Derm Foundation embeddings for dermatology-related tasks achieved significantly higher quality than those built solely on embeddings or fine tuned from BiT-M [SOURCE 4]
UsefulnessEfficacy.TestType: The model was evaluated for data-efficient accuracy across skin-related classification tasks [SOURCE 1]
UsefulnessEfficacy.TestingDataDescription: The model was tested by training a linear classifier on Derm-Foundations embeddings and comparing its performance to a standard BiT-M model [SOURCE 1]
